title: Staying Safe Online
tagline: Passwords, scams, and protecting your personal information.
description: Learn the habits that keep your phone, your accounts and your money safe. We cover strong passwords, scam messages, and what not to share with strangers online.
outcomes: Make a strong password you can remember
Spot the red flags in a scam message
Lock your phone with a PIN
Know what to do if you are tricked

lessons.title: Making a strong password you can remember
lessons.body:
A strong password is long and hard for others to guess, but easy for you to remember.

## Use a sentence
Pick three or four words that mean something to you, like: MangoTree Kitwe 2009 Rain. Join them together: MangoTreeKitwe2009Rain. That is long, strong and memorable.

## Avoid these
Do not use your name, your birthday, 1234, or the word password. Do not use the same password for everything. If one account is stolen, the others stay safe.
key_points: Use three or four words together
Use a different password for each account
lessons.try_it: Think of four words you will remember and write a practice password on paper. Do not use it for a real account yet.

lessons.title: Red flags of scam messages
lessons.body:
Scammers send messages that look real to trick you into giving money or your PIN.

## Common red flags
The message says you have won a prize you never entered. It says your account will be closed unless you act now. It asks for your PIN or a code sent to your phone. The sender is a number you do not know, or the spelling is strange.

## What to do
Stop. Do not reply, do not click links, do not send money. Call the company on its official number to check. Delete the message and warn your family.
key_points: Real companies never ask for your PIN
Urgent pressure is a warning sign
Do not click links from strangers
Check by calling the official number
lessons.try_it: Look through your SMS messages. Can you find one that has a red flag?

lessons.title: Lock your phone with a PIN
lessons.body:
If your phone is lost or stolen, a lock stops others from reading your messages or using your mobile money.

## Set a lock
Open Settings, tap Security or Lock screen, then choose PIN. Pick 4 to 6 numbers that are not your birthday. Type it twice to confirm.
key_points: A PIN protects your messages and money
Do not share your PIN, even with friends
lessons.try_it: Set a screen lock PIN on your phone today.

lessons.title: Check what you learned
lessons.body: Answer these short questions about staying safe.

quiz.question: Which password is the strongest?
quiz.explanation: Long passwords made of several words are much harder to guess, and still easy for you to remember.

quiz.question: A message says your account will close unless you send your PIN. What should you do?
options: Ignore it and call the official number
quiz.explanation: Real companies never ask for your PIN. Call the official number if you are worried.
